item.title: Intelligent and Trustworthy Web Information Systems
item.content:encoded:
Junhui Zhao, Beijing Jiaotong University

Jiaheng Wang, Southeast University

Hong Zhao, Tsinghua University

The Web ecosystem faces interconnected challenges to trust spanning technical vulnerabilities, content manipulation, and regulatory compliance. System-level attacks and data breaches are compounded by the ease with which generative AI enables mass production of false content. Simultaneously, regulations like the Digital Services Act and AI Act demand new levels of platform accountability and content moderation that conventional governance cannot support, creating an urgent need for integrated solutions.

This special issue seeks research on intelligent and trustworthy Web information systems addressing three interconnected themes: Web security, content integrity, and online discourse governance. The research should span six dimensions of trustworthiness including security, privacy, explainability, fairness, robustness and accountable human oversight. The call welcomes original research and review articles that integrate Web security techniques, content monitoring systems, AI-based detection methods, and platform governance approaches to build a trustworthy Web ecosystem.

item.title: Understanding Tensions in Digital Supply Chain Ecosystems
item.content:encoded:
Robert Glenn Richey, Jr., Auburn University

Tarun Agrawal, Chalmers University of Technology

Jag Srai, University of Cambridge

Medo Pournader, University of Melbourne

Organizations in digital supply chain ecosystems face conflicting demands: enhancing data sharing and coordination while protecting proprietary information and managing platform dependencies. Digital transformation restructures supply chains from linear, firm-centric models into interconnected ecosystems where control and decision-making are distributed across multiple participants.

This Special Issue applies the responsiveness view to examine how digital supply chain ecosystems reshape coordination when organizations must adjust behaviors across technological boundaries. It explores how ecosystem participants leverage digital visibility for coordinated action while mitigating cybersecurity and strategic vulnerabilities.

The Special Issue welcomes diverse methodological approaches including conceptual, quantitative, and longitudinal research that deepens understanding of responsiveness in digitally mediated supply chains. Contributions should advance theory while providing guidance for designing ecosystems that balance responsiveness, security, sustainability, and value creation.

item.title: The Challenges of Social Media Influencers: AI Integration, Strategic Agency, and New Business Models in Global-Local Digital Markets
item.content:encoded:
Raffaele Filieri, Audencia Business School

Elmira Djafarova, Northumbria University

Margot Racat, IDRAC Business School

Veronika Keller, Szechenyi Istvan University

Rickard Enstroem, MacEwan University

Social media influencer marketing faces uncertainty amid algorithm fatigue, regulatory scrutiny, declining consumer trust, and AI-generated influencers. Traditional theoretical frameworks struggle to explain how AI content, algorithmic curation, and synthetic personas reshape influence dynamics.

This special issue examines whether traditional influencer marketing is ending or undergoing paradigm shift in how influence is constructed, monetized, and governed. It explores how authenticity, artificial intelligence, and algorithmic mediation intersect to reshape influence practices while addressing emerging regulatory frameworks.

The issue welcomes empirically grounded contributions from multiple disciplines including strategy, media studies, consumer behavior, and technology management. It particularly encourages interdisciplinary, globally inclusive research examining non-Western contexts, emerging platforms, and underrepresented influencer communities.

item.title: Critical Perspectives on Digital Platform Ecosystems: Governance, Influence, and Consequences
item.content:encoded:
Chayanin Wipusanawan, University of Passau

Andreas König, University of Passau

Jan Krämer, University of Passau

Hemant Bhargava, University of California Davis

This special issue examines digital platform ecosystems and their multifaceted effects on economies and societies. As platforms increasingly mediate work, communication, information access, and public participation, understanding their design, governance, and regulation becomes essential. The collection invites scholarly work addressing both the innovative potential and the societal challenges posed by these powerful intermediaries.

The special issue welcomes theoretical and empirical contributions employing diverse methodologies across information systems and related disciplines. Research may explore governance mechanisms, competitive dynamics, innovation structures, content moderation, equity concerns, regulatory frameworks, and platform effects in different economic contexts. All contributions undergo double-blind peer review.
